display.title: Episode 483: The King Is Watching (Rosh Chodesh Tammuz)
display.summary_short: A coachman tries to pick apples from the king's orchard, and the rabbi on lookout cries 'He's watching!', meaning the King of all kings. Plus a Rosh Chodesh Tammuz message.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on the eve of Rosh Chodesh Tammuz, as the show reaches program number 483 after ten years on the air. Uncle Yossi marvels that grown-ups still tune in, even in their cars on the way home, and hopes that saying the Shema together leads listeners to more mitzvos, since one mitzvah brings another. After the Hakochainik march, a returning young guest says the Shema and one of the Twelve Pesukim, and everyone gives tzedakah. The story, on the theme that good character and honesty come before Torah, follows old Rabbi Yitzchak on a long wagon ride through a forest. His hungry coachman wants to climb into the king's apple orchard and asks the rabbi to keep watch. Just as he reaches the top of the fence, the rabbi calls out 'He's watching!' and the coachman flees, only to learn that the One watching was the King of all kings, Who commanded 'You shall not steal'. Uncle Yossi then explains that Rosh Chodesh is the 'head' of the month, so good resolutions made then shape the whole month, and gives candle-lighting time.
display.lesson: Hashem is always watching, so be honest and never take what is not yours, even when no person can see.

date.note: 'Tonight is Rosh Chodesh... the new month is Tammuz' (evening of 29 Sivan begins 30 Sivan, Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 5751); program number 483 stated on air; candle lighting 8:10. A Tuesday.

sources_cited.note: 'Know what is above you: an eye that sees', so you will not come to sin.
